title: Rational Identification Degree of Effects in Dense One-Factor Gaussian DAGs
banked_reason: Only ten of 47 reported misses are resolved, while the exact global D6 frontier and extremal orbits remain open; the sound delivered package achieves incremental rather than the field floor.
gap_reasons: The promised audit of all 47 reported misses is not delivered: only ten chart formulas are supplied, while formulas or exact nonrationality certificates for the remaining 37 are explicitly open; complete that ledger (and the negative-label audit) or narrow the advertised deliverable.

The promised exact D6 frontier is replaced by a preliminary graph-692 interval (3 through 12): no all-edge census, global upper certificate, exact extremal degree, or extremal orbit is supplied; deliver those matching certificates or re-scope the central claim to the local chart and interval results.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a one-parent sink lifting result, produced exact rational charts for ten reported gaps, and certified the graph-692 lower bound excluding degree at most two; the math referee passed these limited claims and both cited asymptotic lemmas were source-attested. The field-level program collapsed because 37 classes and the negative-label audit remained unresolved, while graph 692 retained only the interval 3–12 rather than an exact degree or global D6 extremal certificate. A future re-raise should reuse the certificate generator and chart artifacts, but must complete the census and quotient-aware degree minimization rather than restate the local results.
tldr: For six-observed-node dense one-source Gaussian DAGs, the note gives a universal one-parent sink chart and explicit rational effects for ten reported algorithm gaps. A replayable finite-field minor excludes degree-at-most-two covariance quotients for \(1\to2\) in \(G_{692}\); its separate sink chart gives \(3\le d(G_{692},1\to2)\le12\). The exact degree, full edgewise census, and global \(D_6\) remain open.
gap: The closest combined sufficient algorithm leaves 47 reported whole-graph positives without formulas, subject to qualified algebraic labels. Hollering, Misra and Sturma (2026) optimize adaptive identifying-polynomial degree for acyclic mixed graphs; a one-edge rank-one example separates total polynomial and covariance-quotient degrees by the target-variable degree shift, but the sharp relation and any additional adaptive savings remain unresolved. The published work does not supply a certified six-node covariance-quotient frontier.
fill: Build an exact orbit ledger, settle the remaining reported gaps and negative labels, minimize formulas modulo the covariance ideal, establish the relation to adaptive identifying-polynomial degree on the same rank-one kernel, and prove matching upper/lower certificates for the global edgewise D6 frontier. First seek characteristic-zero identities or obstructions for representative eight- and nine-edge gaps, then scale the edgewise census to graphs with more than nine edges.
